name: Lucian Gable
preparty_markdown:
Lucian designed the physical experience of Treasures of the World: every wall angle, sight line, spotlight,

pedestal, and dramatic reveal. He is tasteful, exacting, and deeply convinced that visitors would behave

better if they understood circulation. He has strong opinions about fonts, cords, and anything that interrupts

a clean visual field.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Aesthetic, controlled, mildly pretentious in a lovable way, easily offended by bad placement rather than bad manners.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Creative rival of sculptor Malcolm Carrara after a very public argument about scale.

• Works constantly with Riley Bloom, who keeps trying to add flowers where Lucian designed negative space.

• Rafael Gilt has veto power over several of Lucian's more adventurous display ideas.

COSTUME

Architectural formalwear: monochrome suit, turtleneck with jacket, sharply cut black attire, interesting glasses, rolled plans

or a small laser measure prop.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“That is not empty space. It is intentional restraint.”

“If you put a chair there, the entire room becomes dishonest.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

name: Vivienne Marrow
preparty_markdown:
Vivienne moves between embassies, museums, ministries, and negotiation tables where everyone insists the

issue is 'purely cultural' while bringing three lawyers. She is poised, persuasive, and very difficult to rush.

Her work focuses on contested cultural property and long-term international loans.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Elegant, diplomatic, strategic, warm until precision is required. You can disagree without ever sounding flustered.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Long-running professional friendship and rivalry with Helena Cross.

• Frequently debates Marcus Pryce and Juno March on how restitution should actually work.

• Adrian Vellum has courted her support for several international partnerships.

COSTUME

Refined diplomatic formalwear; jewel tones, elegant suit or dress, subtle cultural or heritage-inspired accessory worn

respectfully. Optional slim portfolio.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Diplomacy is the art of saying 'absolutely not' in six agreeable sentences.”

“A long-term loan is not the same thing as forgetting where something came from.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

name: Theo Glass
preparty_markdown:
Theo made a fortune building software and has spent the last five years trying to become the sort of collector

whose taste is discussed rather than merely his net worth. He is enthusiastic, competitive, and genuinely

knowledgeable enough to resent anyone who assumes otherwise. His collection mixes contemporary art,

design, and objects he describes as 'historically underpriced.'

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Energetic, socially confident, competitive, eager to demonstrate taste without looking eager.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Buys through Grant Easel more often than either admits.

• Runs in the same social orbit as Sienna Voss and Daphne Palette.

• Morgan Slate once described his collection as 'an algorithm discovering patina,' which Theo has not forgotten.

COSTUME

Modern black tie with tech-founder looseness: excellent jacket, minimal sneakers or polished shoes, unusual watch, bold

glasses. Optional auction paddle as a joke prop.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“I liked it before the catalogue essay explained why.”

“Collecting is not shopping. Shopping has return policies.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.
